title: Senior Director, Commercial, EU Center
description:
Mavericks Wanted 

When was the last time you achieved the impossible? If that thought feels overwhelming, you might want to pause here, but if it sparks excitement...read on 
 
In 2015, we pioneered a “moneyball for biotech” approach, pooling projects and promising early-stage research from academia together under one financial umbrella to reduce risk and unleash innovation. This model allows science and small teams of experts to lead the way. We build bridges to groundbreaking advancements in rare disease, and develop life-changing medicines for patients with unmet needs as fast as humanly possible.  
 
Together we define white space, push boundaries, and empower people to solve problems. If you're someone who defies convention, join us and work alongside some of the most respected minds in the industry. Together, we'll ask "why not?" and help reengineer the future of biopharma. At BridgeBio, we value curiosity and experimentation—including the ethical & thoughtful use of AI to improve clarity, speed, and quality of work. 

What You’ll Do

You will report to the VP & GM EU Center and work closely with Medical Affairs, Market Access, Patient Advocacy, Supply Chain and Finance, as well as global commercial teams, to drive strategic initiatives that support BridgeBio’s mission of delivering transformative medicines to patients with genetic diseases and genetically driven cancers. Your primary purpose will be to build and lead the commercial organisation in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, preparing and executing the launches in ADH1 and achondroplasia and building the foundation for future indications. You will lead the field force, including Disease Network Specialists who will move into Key Account Manager roles after launch, and drive the local adaptation of disease awareness and marketing materials, the local execution of customer service offerings, and forecasting and demand planning, with a focus on pre-launch readiness in 2027, followed by launch execution and growth. This role requires effective collaboration with cross-functional colleagues and external stakeholders to ensure high-quality execution and impact. The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in rare disease commercial leadership and launch execution with strong communication skills, adaptability, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, hands-on environment.

Responsibilities

  • Field force leadership: Build, lead and develop the commercial field team across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, including the move from pre-launch disease education to key account management after launch
  • Launch readiness and execution: Own the commercial launch plans for ADH1 and achondroplasia in each country, and set up a model that can take on future indications
  • Local marketing adaptation: Adapt global disease awareness and marketing materials to local needs, languages and regulations, and take them through local review and approval
  • Customer service offerings: Ensure flawless local execution of HCP service offerings, together with Medical Affairs and external vendors
  • Forecasting and demand planning: Own the local forecast and demand plan, align it with Supply Chain and Finance, and track performance against plan
  • Cross-functional partnership: Work closely with Medical Affairs, Market Access and Patient Advocacy so that launch, access and field activities are coordinated in each country
  • Compliance and governance: Make sure all commercial activities comply with HWG, the Austrian Medicines Act (AMG), the Swiss Therapeutic Products Act (HMG) and the industry codes in each country, and that clear boundaries are kept with medical activities

Where You’ll Work

  • This is a field-based leadership role based in Germany, ideally in the Munich area, covering Germany, Austria and Switzerland
  • Approximately 50% travel is anticipated for field visits, customer meetings, congresses and internal meetings, including regular visits to our Zug office

Who You Are

  • Degree in life sciences, pharmacy, medicine or business. An advanced degree (MBA, PhD, PharmD) is a plus
  • At least 12 years of commercial experience in pharma or biotech, including at least 5 years leading field teams, ideally in rare diseases, endocrinology or paediatrics
  • Proven track record of at least one successful launch in Germany, ideally a rare disease or orphan drug launch, with experience in Austria and/or Switzerland a strong plus
  • Positive, inspiring and tenacious leader, experienced in biotech build-out environments, solution-driven and hands-on, with high integrity
  • Solid knowledge of forecasting, demand planning and P&L management, and of how pricing and reimbursement (AMNOG, EKO, SL) shape the commercial plan
  • Comfortable using digital engagement channels and driving productivity with AI tools
  • Fluent German, and fluent English to work effectively with international and US-based colleagues
  • Willingness to travel approximately 50% of the time

 

Rewarding Those Who Make the Mission Possible

  • We have high expectations for our team members. We make sure those working hard for patients are rewarded and cared for in return.
  • Market leading compensation
  • Hybrid work model - we value your flexibility in how you work, but encourage time in the office to strengthen our culture, collaboration, and sense of community

Mission Brief 

As LCA & Environmental Data Specialist, you will establish our Life Cycle Assessment and environmental data capabilities from the ground up. Your mission is to create a reliable environmental data foundation, conduct Life Cycle Assessments in accordance with recognized standards and translate complex environmental data into meaningful insights. You will work closely with Engineering, Procurement, Manufacturing, Testing, Infrastructure and other teams to understand the environmental impact of our product throughout its lifecycle.

 

Your Role in Our Space Mission:

  • LCA Methodology & Modelling: Define goal and scope, develop Life Cycle Inventories, perform impact assessments, interpret results and document assumptions, limitations, and methodological choices. 
  • Environmental Data Collection: Collaborate closely with Engineering, Procurement, Manufacturing, Infrastructure and Testing to actively collect and understand the environmental, operational, material and supplier data required for LCA. 
  • Environmental Data Management: Establish structured and scalable processes for environmental data, ensuring data quality, consistency, completeness and traceability. 
  • LCA Tools & Databases: Develop and maintain LCA models, datasets and Life Cycle Inventories in openLCA and relevant LCA databases. 
  • Environmental Impact Analysis: Analyse LCA results, identify environmental hotspots and improvement opportunities and translate complex results into clear and actionable insights.

description:
Mission Brief 

As Director of Production Engineering, you are accountable for the end-to-end production engineering capability across all manufacturing operations. Your mission is to industrialize development outputs into repeatable, scalable, and compliant serial production, ensuring manufacturing readiness, process stability, quality, cost efficiency, and on-time delivery. You lead the team that converts early procedures into robust production standards, embeds them in PLM/MES systems, and drives continuous improvement across the factory.

You act as the primary interface between Engineering (design & development) and Manufacturing (production & operations)—ensuring requirements, procedures, tooling, documentation, test strategies, and digital manufacturing infrastructure are aligned for high-rate, high-quality execution. 

Your Role in Our Space Mission: 

1) Production engineering strategy & leadership

  • Define and execute the production engineering roadmap, including industrialization strategy, standardization, and scalability for serial production.
  • Lead and develop a team of production/process/manufacturing engineers; set goals, coaching plans, hiring needs, and performance standards.
  • Establish clear governance for process ownership, engineering change implementation, and cross-functional decision-making.

2) Assembly, integration & test (AIT) process ownership

  • Own manufacturing process definition across:
    • Assembly: mechanical/electrical build procedures, torque specs, critical process parameters, work instructions.
    • Integration: subsystem integration strategy (e.g., avionics, propulsion, communications), sequencing, interfaces, and acceptance criteria.
    • Testing: functional, subsystem, and system-level test strategy; test readiness, execution plans, and troubleshooting methodology.
  • Ensure processes are repeatable, auditable, and optimized for safety, throughput, and quality.

3) Industrialization & manufacturing readiness (NPI / transfer to production)

  • Coordinate with development teams to receive initial procedures and convert them into production-ready standards (control plans, critical-to-quality characteristics where relevant).
  • Drive manufacturing readiness reviews, line readiness, and process qualification for new products, variants, or upgrades.
  • Lead the “first builds”/pilot runs, capturing learnings and stabilizing procedures for volume execution.

4) Digital manufacturing (PLM/MES) & configuration control

  • Own the production engineering contribution to PLM/MES:
    • Translate procedures into structured digital work instructions.
    • Ensure traceability, configuration control, and alignment of as-built data.
  • Oversee creation and maintenance of:
    • mBOM (Manufacturing Bill of Materials)
    • BOP (Bill of Process)
    • Routings, work centers, and data collection points for quality and traceability.
  • Ensure engineering changes are implemented cleanly and quickly, with minimal disruption to production.

5) Documentation, compliance & quality partnership

  • Ensure complete, consistent documentation for:
    • Work instructions, process specifications, test reports, NCRs (non-conformance reports), deviations/waivers, and as-built configurations.
  • Partner with Quality to build robust nonconformance management and corrective action systems (root cause, containment, RCCA & PA).
  • Ensure processes meet applicable regulatory, customer, and internal compliance requirements.

6) Cross-functional execution & production support

  • Serve as senior escalation point for technical blockers in production: diagnose recurring issues, direct corrective actions, and prevent reoccurrence.
  • Align with Supply Chain and Operations on:
    • Kitting strategy, material availability, critical path timelines, and constraint removal.
  • Coordinate engineering support coverage and readiness for shifts, rate increases, and critical campaigns.

7) Continuous improvement, cost & throughput

  • Support Lean Team on Lean/CI initiatives to improve:
    • Yield, cycle time, takt adherence, OEE, scrap/rework reduction, and labor efficiency.
  • Establish KPIs and operating mechanisms (tier meetings, weekly business reviews) to track and improve production engineering performance.
  • Build business cases for capital investments (test equipment, tooling, automation) and manage the budget for your scope.

8) Capability building: training & knowledge management

  • Build a strong knowledge-transfer system between engineers and technicians:
    • Training plans, certification matrices, standardized visual work instructions, and lessons-learned libraries.
  • Ensure procedures are systematically categorized, version-controlled, and easily accessible to production teams.

Success measures (typical KPIs)

  • Improved first-pass yield, reduced NCR rate, reduced rework hours
  • Reduced cycle time and improved on-time delivery
  • Faster and cleaner engineering change implementation
  • Increased process stability (fewer repeat issues, fewer line stops)
  • Strong audit outcomes and complete traceability / as-built compliance
  • High team engagement, retention, and capability maturity

Qualification Checklist 

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Aerospace, Automotive, Industrial Engineering, or similar.
  • Significant experience in production/manufacturing engineering, industrialization, manufacturing operations—ideally across complex electromechanical systems.
  • Proven leadership experience managing teams and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Demonstrated ability in troubleshooting and structured problem solving (e.g., 8D, Ishikawa, 5-Why).
  • Solid project/program management skills: prioritization, risk management, schedule ownership.
  • Fluent English; German or other languages depending on site needs.

title: Senior Product Specialist Partner Solutions Architect
description:
A newly created role to help Databricks create new product categories. As Databricks accelerates its most strategic products, we are investing ahead of the curve in the partner ecosystem that helps our customers adopt them, and we are building a new specialisation function to lead that effort. You will pioneer it across EMEA.

Reporting to: Director, Partner Field Engineering (EMEA).

As the Senior Product Specialist Partner Solutions Architect, you own how our leading System Integrator partners develop deep, market-leading expertise in Databricks' priority products:

  • OLTP/Postgres (Lakebase): Databricks' fully managed, Postgres-compatible operational (OLTP) database for intelligent applications
  • Product AI (Genie): Databricks' natural-language analytics experience, letting anyone ask questions of governed data conversationally
  • AI Router & Governance (Unity Gateway): Databricks' governed gateway for securely managing, monitoring and routing access to AI and large language model endpoints
  • Migrations & Modernisation: moving legacy data warehouses and platforms onto the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform
  • Turn-key Solutions: Cybersecurity (Lakewatch) and CDP (CustomerLake) with more to come

Your mandate is to take our leading partners to the highest tier of Centre-of-Excellence product specialisation on these products, and to turn them into independent, market-leading extensions of the Databricks field. Working hand in hand with our EMEA Product Specialist team, you will carry both the deep technical narrative and the business-value and go-to-market narrative that get these products positioned, adopted and scaled through the partner channel. This is a builder's role: you will design the blueprint for a partner product-specialist function that Databricks scales globally, starting in EMEA.

What we are trying to achieve

Databricks' priority products are seeing strong momentum across EMEA. Lakebase is one of the fastest-growing additions to our platform, Unity Gateway is newly generally available, and AI/BI + Genie are changing how customers work with their data. As adoption accelerates, our partners are central to helping customers realise value quickly and at scale. Deepening partner expertise in these products is one of the most powerful levers we have to accelerate customer time-to-value, and this role exists to build that capability deliberately and ahead of demand, so our partners lead the market.

What the role owns

  • Building the partner specialist community (the day-to-day). Select, enable and certify leading EMEA partners to the highest tier of product specialisation, running the enablement engine end to end: partner selection, technical upskilling to expert depth, certification and first joint customer wins.
  • Partnering with our Product Specialist team. Act as the partner-side counterpart to Databricks' EMEA Product Specialists, bringing the latest product expertise to partners, connecting partner enablement to live customer opportunities, and channelling partner and customer adoption insight back to our product organisation.
  • Scaling specialist capacity through partners. Grow models where specialised partners bring product-specialist capacity to joint customers, so expertise scales across the ecosystem.
  • Launch-partner motions. Position specialised partners as launch partners for major product releases, signalling ecosystem trust and accelerating go-to-market at each milestone.
  • Thought leadership and the business-value narrative. Author the "better-together" technical and commercial story for these products in the partner channel: reference architectures, positioning, partner offers and value framing that let partners sell and deliver independently. Be a visible voice for partner product specialisation, internally and externally.
  • Building the function. Define the operating model, the specialisation and certification criteria, the partner selection bar and the cadence, and create the template Databricks adopts to scale this function worldwide.

The impact you will have

  • Accelerate customer adoption and time-to-value on Databricks' priority products by putting genuine product depth into the partner channel.
  • Grow partner-led momentum behind our fastest-growing products, building partner capability ahead of the demand curve.
  • Elevate leading EMEA System Integrators to full independence on the priority products, so they operate as market leaders and true extensions of the Databricks field.
  • Establish a repeatable, globally scalable partner product-specialist function, proven in EMEA and exported across Databricks.

What we look for

  • Extensive hands-on experience with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, with genuine depth in at least two of the priority products above and the ability to get to depth quickly on the rest. This is a senior role for an established Databricks expert.
  • Proven ability to build partner or field capability at scale: enablement, certification and community-building that turns others into independent experts.
  • Strong business-value and go-to-market instinct: able to translate technical depth into commercial positioning and partner-led market impact, and to engage partner and customer organisations at senior-executive level.
  • Demonstrated thought leadership: authoring technical and business content (reference architectures, solution guides, positioning, playbooks) and presenting complex products credibly to technical and executive audiences.
  • At least 5 years of technical pre-sales or sales-methodology experience in a consumption business model, and experience designing and delivering end-to-end data, warehousing and AI architectures.
  • Coding experience in a core language (Python, SQL, Java or Scala) and hands-on experience building data applications or AI agents.
  • The maturity to build a new function from the ground up: defining the operating model, standards and cadence, and managing multiple changing priorities across a partner ecosystem and internal teams.

Nice to have: System Integrator or consulting background; experience with transactional databases (e.g. PostgreSQL) and application development; experience with LLM gateways, AI governance or AI security; experience running partner specialisation, certification or champion programmes; additional European languages.

The role requires up to 40% travel across EMEA, to partner sites, Databricks offices and key industry events.

About Databricks

Databricks is the Data and AI company. title: 3D Computer Vision Research Engineer - World Map
description: About Niantic Spatial AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time. That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are. In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right. Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us. About the Role You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. This is an end-to-end applied research role that spans from strong engineering and data-systems work to R&D in 3D deep learning, transformers, and foundation models. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems. The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves. You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable engineering — developing new approaches to geospatial registration, correspondence, and geometric optimization, then productionizing these technologies to directly improve Niantic Spatial's world model. What You'll Do Geospatial Registration — Develop and advance algorithms for world-scale georeferencing and registration across imagery, 3D reconstructions, point clouds, and geographic reference data. 3D Geometry & Correspondence — Build and improve methods spanning multi-view geometry, SfM, SLAM, feature matching, learned correspondence, bundle adjustment, point-cloud registration, and ICP. Data & Evaluation — Create the data and evaluation flywheel for world-scale mapping — design and maintain large-scale datasets, pipelines, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies that expose hard failure modes, accelerate research iteration, and support production. Learning-Based 3D Reasoning — Explore and develop learning-based approaches for geospatial understanding, combining transformers and 3D foundation models with geometric priors and uncertainty modeling. Production Robustness — Design robust solutions for challenging real-world conditions: sparse or noisy GPS, changing appearance, inconsistent reconstruction quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps. Cross-Functional Collaboration — Partner with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping — as well as engineering and product teams — to identify high-impact problems and turn research breakthroughs into end-to-end production systems. Research Communication — Share results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, and internal presentations; contribute to publications and open research where appropriate. What You'll Bring Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Photogrammetry, or a closely related field — or equivalent research or industry experience. Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, machine learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related area. Demonstrated experience with 3D geometry and several relevant areas — multi-view reconstruction, SfM, SLAM, camera pose estimation, point-cloud registration, image-based localization, georeferencing, or sensor fusion. The ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose the right mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously. Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML and scientific-computing libraries (PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy). Strong software engineering skills — you can turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems. A track record of taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data. Clear written and verbal communication; able to collaborate effectively across research and engineering disciplines. Nice to Have PhD in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, photogrammetry, geodesy, remote sensing, or a related field — not required, but valued. A strong publication record or active involvement in the research community at venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, SIGGRAPH, 3DV, ICRA, or RSS. Experience with learning-based approaches for visual or 3D understanding — transformers, point transformers, foundation models, or methods combining learned representations with explicit geometric priors. Experience with aerial or satellite imagery, GNSS/GPS, geodesy, mapping systems, or large-scale spatial data. Evidence of technical leadership, mentorship, or successful cross-functional delivery. Compensation & Benefits Base salary: Competitive market rate. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package. Location & Work Model This role is based in our London office, with three days per week in office. We welcome applications from candidates who require visa sponsorship. Inclusive Application We know the strongest candidates don't always tick every box. raw.title: 3D Computer Vision Research Engineer - World Map
raw.description:
About Niantic Spatial

AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.

About the Role

You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. This is an end-to-end applied research role that spans from strong engineering and data-systems work to R&D in 3D deep learning, transformers, and foundation models. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems.

The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves.

You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable engineering — developing new approaches to geospatial registration, correspondence, and geometric optimization, then productionizing these technologies to directly improve Niantic Spatial's world model.

What You'll Do

  • Geospatial Registration — Develop and advance algorithms for world-scale georeferencing and registration across imagery, 3D reconstructions, point clouds, and geographic reference data.

  • 3D Geometry & Correspondence — Build and improve methods spanning multi-view geometry, SfM, SLAM, feature matching, learned correspondence, bundle adjustment, point-cloud registration, and ICP.

  • Data & Evaluation — Create the data and evaluation flywheel for world-scale mapping — design and maintain large-scale datasets, pipelines, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies that expose hard failure modes, accelerate research iteration, and support production.

  • Learning-Based 3D Reasoning — Explore and develop learning-based approaches for geospatial understanding, combining transformers and 3D foundation models with geometric priors and uncertainty modeling.

  • Production Robustness — Design robust solutions for challenging real-world conditions: sparse or noisy GPS, changing appearance, inconsistent reconstruction quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration — Partner with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping — as well as engineering and product teams — to identify high-impact problems and turn research breakthroughs into end-to-end production systems.

  • Research Communication — Share results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, and internal presentations; contribute to publications and open research where appropriate.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Photogrammetry, or a closely related field — or equivalent research or industry experience.

  • Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, machine learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related area.

  • Demonstrated experience with 3D geometry and several relevant areas — multi-view reconstruction, SfM, SLAM, camera pose estimation, point-cloud registration, image-based localization, georeferencing, or sensor fusion.

  • The ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose the right mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously.

  • Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML and scientific-computing libraries (PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy).

  • Strong software engineering skills — you can turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems.

  • A track record of taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data.

  • Clear written and verbal communication; able to collaborate effectively across research and engineering disciplines.

Nice to Have

  • PhD in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, photogrammetry, geodesy, remote sensing, or a related field — not required, but valued.

  • A strong publication record or active involvement in the research community at venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, SIGGRAPH, 3DV, ICRA, or RSS.

  • Experience with learning-based approaches for visual or 3D understanding — transformers, point transformers, foundation models, or methods combining learned representations with explicit geometric priors.

  • Experience with aerial or satellite imagery, GNSS/GPS, geodesy, mapping systems, or large-scale spatial data.

  • Evidence of technical leadership, mentorship, or successful cross-functional delivery.

More and more of that business is now run by AI agents, and we want you to help build them. These aren't chatbots. Our agents have real jobs: They inspect boards. They watch the factory. They spot stray parts in robot storage, diagnose printer faults and clear stuck machines. They run the back office. They book supplier invoices, chase late orders, explain quotes and triage bugs. They write our code. Most of what our team ships starts in an agent session. LOCATION: King's Cross, London · PATTERN: Lab-based, full-time

The opportunity

We're a stealth startup in AI and bio, building infrastructure for data generation. The team is small and elite, the problems are hard, and the foundations are being laid right now. You'd help write them from the first line, with real ownership and a direct line to the founders.

This role covers the cell side of our protein characterisation work. You would keep the cell lines healthy and run the assays that show how a designed protein behaves on a living cell, week after week, to the same standard.

About us

AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one.

We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team.

The role

You will run cell culture and the cell-based assays for our protein characterisation work. That means the mammalian lines the assays depend on, from thaw through routine passage to a banked and documented stock, and the weekly rhythm of seeding, treating, reading and reporting plates.

Most of it runs in 384-well plates with imaging-based or flow cytometry readouts. You will run those assays as designed, with the controls and replicates that make a curve defensible, and you will be the person who notices when a plate, a line or a reagent lot has started to drift.

Assay design and the shape of the cascade sit with the scientist who leads this work today, so you are not being asked to invent the panel. You are being asked to make it run the same way every week, to record what you did in a form the rest of the system can read, and to tighten the protocols as they settle, including moving them towards the plate formats our automation will take on.

Your first 90 days

FIRST 30 DAYS

◆ Take over routine culture and banking for the protein cell lines, working to the protocols we already run.

◆ Learn the panel end to end by running each assay alongside the scientist who owns it.

DAYS 30 TO 60

◆ Run at least one assay in the panel independently, including its controls and acceptance criteria.

◆ Revise one culture or assay protocol so that someone else could follow it without asking you.

DAYS 60 TO 90

◆ Hold the weekly assay schedule on your own and return results on the agreed turnaround.

◆ Bring one protocol to a tighter precision bar, or into a plate format ready for automation.

Who you are

You are a hands-on cell biologist who takes assay variability personally. You have run the same assay often enough to tell a real effect from a bad plate, and you would rather find the cause than repeat the run.

The week has a rhythm in this job: cells to feed, plates to seed, runs to finish, numbers to return. You are happy with that, you keep records someone else can pick up, and you say early when something looks wrong rather than at the end of the week.

We do not hire people into boxes. The team is small, and early hires here end up owning work beyond the job they joined for. Nobody arrives with every part of this role. If you are strong in most of it and quick to learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

MUST HAVE

◆ Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture: adherent and suspension lines, aseptic technique, and thawing, passaging and banking to a high and consistent standard.

◆ Experience running cell-based assays end to end, including relevant controls, replicates and dose-response curves behind a reported number.

◆ Comfort with plate-based work and the arithmetic that goes with it, such as dilution series, plate maps and normalisation.

◆ Careful, traceable record-keeping that someone else can follow without asking you.

◆ A PhD in cell biology, pharmacology, immunology or a related field, or an MSc and two to three years of relevant lab experience.

NICE TO HAVE

◆ Reporter cell line bioassays for binding or blockade.

◆ Receptor internalisation, lysosomal trafficking or cytotoxicity assays.

◆ High-content or fluorescence imaging, and the image analysis behind it.

◆ 384-well formats, liquid handlers or other plate-based automation.

◆ Flow cytometry, for example for surface receptor quantification.

Why this is unusual

Most cell-based assay roles sit inside a discovery project. You build an assay, you answer a question with it, and the assay goes quiet. This one is closer to running an instrument. The same assays run every week against a stream of new molecules, and the number that comes out is the product.

That changes what good looks like. Precision matters more than novelty, a protocol is only finished when someone else can run it and get your answer, and every passage, plate and reagent lot is captured as structured data, because a result is only as trustworthy as the cells behind it.

Some people find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing in advance which one you are.

How we work

This is a lab-based role at our site in King's Cross, London. The cells are in the lab, so most of your week will be too, with room for writing and analysis away from the bench. The wider team is distributed and travels, so you will work with people who are not always in the building.

We work in the open. Decisions are written down, work happens centrally rather than scattered across tools, and the week opens with a session the whole company attends. There is a quarterly offsite. Each person owns their area and makes the call inside it, and we will expect that of you early rather than late.

UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover. More is added as the team grows.

The team you will join

You will join the protein characterisation team and report to its lead. Day to day you will work with the scientist who designs the assay cascade, with the protein production and molecular characterisation scientists upstream of you, with the functional genomics team who share the cell culture suite, and with the engineers building the software and automation the lab runs on.

We are a small, elite team, and this is the first seat given entirely to the cell-based side of the work.

Our process

Our process has four stages. A short screening call about the role and the practicalities. A behavioural interview about how you work, run from the same template for every candidate, before anything technical. A technical stage with the protein characterisation team, built around real work rather than a puzzle, including time with us in person at the lab. Then references, aimed at whatever we still want to understand.

If you are not sure whether you match every line above, apply anyway. We would rather read it and decide.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. Applications welcome from candidates of any background.

raw.description:

Sparta is the AI leader for commodity trading, home to Leonidas AI, the first operating system for oil and commodity traders.

Backed by $42 million in Series B funding led by One Peak, with participation from returning investors FirstMark and Singular, the same investors behind AI leaders like Legora, Dataiku, and Synthesia. Most companies are building a chatbot on top of data. We've built an agent with an actual reasoning layer, grounded in years of proprietary market data and in-house trading expertise nobody else has.

We're scaling fast, and it's an exciting time to join. From independents to multinationals, the world's leading commodity teams use Sparta and Leonidas AI to move faster, trade smarter, and stay ahead of the market.

At Sparta, you'll be trusted to take ownership, backed by a team who wants you to succeed. AI is how we build here, not just what we sell. Good ideas move fast, and yours could go from staging to production in a couple of hours, whatever department you're in. You'll be challenged, supported, and given room to grow, building the AI that's changing how commodity trading gets done.

Your work has reach. From shaping Leonidas AI, to powering smarter decisions for traders around the world, to changing how commodity trading is done. And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.

The Role

Location: London or Geneva. In-office, with flexibility for 1–2 days per week from home.

Reporting to the CEO and managing a team of 3 in People, you'll be Sparta's most senior People leader. Working directly with the CEO and leadership team, you'll define and execute the people strategy required to scale the organisation, ensuring we have the leadership, capability, culture and organisational structure necessary to achieve our long-term growth ambitions.

We're looking for someone with the strategic ability to grow into a CPO role as Sparta scales.

You'll be shaping and scaling the People organisation, building the structure, capability and leadership needed to support Sparta's next phase of growth: compensation and levelling, performance, leadership development, hiring and organisation design, while ensuring the overall People strategy remains aligned to business objectives. Much of what this role owns needs to be improved, perfected or redesigned, so you'll be hands-on from day one, building frameworks and running processes personally before you're managing others through them. You'll be central to building a consistent, high-performance culture across our distributed teams globally.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Develop and execute Sparta's global people strategy, ensuring organisational structure, capability, culture and talent are aligned to support the company's growth from Series B through its next stage of scale, whilst balancing local employment, cultural and regulatory considerations

  • Act as a strategic advisor to the CEO, Executive Team and Board on organisational design, leadership capability, succession planning, workforce risks and culture

  • Build our compensation architecture: salary bands, a levelling framework, and a consistent, transparent approach to pay across geographies.

  • Introduce a structured performance process and individual scorecards, so everyone knows what success looks like for them.

  • Build our leadership pipeline through talent reviews, succession planning and management development. Give managers the confidence and authority to make more decisions themselves and address people problems early.

  • Lead organisation design, ensuring Sparta's operating model, spans and layers, leadership structure and workforce planning evolve appropriately as the business scales internationally. Partner with Finance and functional leaders to develop workforce planning and capability strategies that support Sparta's growth objectives

  • Own talent acquisition strategy and delivery. Work with Marketing and the TA team to grow our employer brand so more great people come to us.

  • Own Learning & Development: coaching, training, and levelling up managers and individual contributors

  • Provide executive oversight of workplace and employee experience across all locations. Partner closely with the Executive Team and other leaders to align hiring philosophy, location strategy, and expectations across Sparta's distributed teams

  • Represent People at the leadership table. Raise risks early and make sure stakeholders always know where things stand

What Success Looks Like in Your First Year

  • Executive Team aligned around a clear people strategy

  • Leadership effectiveness and manager capability measurably improved

  • Workforce plan linked to business objectives

  • Salary bands and a levelling framework live

  • Individual scorecards in place, so everyone knows what success looks like for them

  • A structured performance review running company-wide, with buy-in from key stakeholders

  • A middle-management empowerment programme in place, with managers visibly making more decisions without escalating to the exec team

  • Succession plans in place for key roles

  • Hiring on track against plan, with quality and retention holding up

About You

  • You've been the most senior People leader in a scaling organisation, or held a Director or VP People role with significant strategic accountability

  • You've worked in a Series B–D SaaS or tech scaleup and know the people challenges of that stage first-hand

  • You've personally built compensation, levelling and performance frameworks, and you can point to what you built and the impact it had

  • You can influence founders, boards and senior executives, and challenge constructively when it's needed

  • You're commercially minded. You find workable compromises and build frameworks that fix problems for good

  • You've led organisational change across distributed, multi-country teams, not just rolled out HR programmes. Sparta has people across London, Geneva, Spain, Singapore, Houston, and Dubai - familiarity with local laws, regulations and cultures in these locations is a distinct advantage

  • You take ownership, move with urgency and are comfortable being hands-on

  • You communicate clearly and proactively

  • You want to grow this role into a CPO seat

  • Experience scaling a tech business from around 100 to 300+ people is a big plus

We care more about what you've achieved, and how relevant it is to our stage, than about a specific number of years' experience.

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you.

If it's on you, it's in your control.

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift

Honesty is an expression of care.

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

We're scaling fast, and it's an exciting time to join. From independents to multinationals, the world's leading commodity teams use Sparta and Leonidas AI to move faster, trade smarter, and stay ahead of the market.

At Sparta, you'll be trusted to take ownership, backed by a team who wants you to succeed. AI is how we build here, not just what we sell. Good ideas move fast, and yours could go from staging to production in a couple of hours, whatever department you're in. You'll be challenged, supported, and given room to grow, building the AI that's changing how commodity trading gets done.

Your work has reach. From shaping Leonidas AI, to powering smarter decisions for traders around the world, to changing how commodity trading is done. And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.


At Sparta, we’re on a mission to build the next generation of commodity trading platforms - replacing the fragmented tools that traders typically rely on with a single, powerful dashboard. Our product is a data-driven platform that aggregates real-time feeds from across the commodities domain, transforming them into intuitive, actionable visualisations within one unified interface.

Traders act on what they see in Sparta. That makes reliability a product feature, not an afterthought - and it’s why this role exists.

This is a deliberate 50/50 split. Half your time is backend engineering: designing and building the distributed services and pipelines that move real-time market data through our platform. The other half is reliability engineering: making those systems observable, resilient, and cheap to operate. If you’ve ever shipped a service and then wished you owned how it ran in production, this is that job.

We’ve kept the split explicit rather than tidy. Our Platform Engineering team owns the shared platform, tooling and automation; you’ll be a close partner to them, and the reliability of your own services is yours.

We’re looking for people who thrive in an empowered environment - engineers who are comfortable being given problems to solve rather than solutions to implement. You should enjoy working at pace, value autonomy, and prefer to ask for forgiveness rather than permission.

Whereas Sparta is a remote-first company, for this role we’re looking for someone who values a hybrid working style, which in a typical week could involve spending a couple of days in the office - with flexibility built in.


WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

Backend engineering

  • Design, build and maintain the backend services behind our real-time and analytical data processing.

  • Optimise pipelines and services for low latency, high throughput and scale.

  • Own features end to end, from shaping the approach to running them in production.

  • Contribute to design reviews with a clear view on the trade-offs.

Reliability engineering

  • Own the operational health of your services. Define what healthy means, then measure it.

  • Improve observability, monitoring and alerting in Datadog, so problems surface before a trader notices.

  • Take part in incident response, then close the loop on the root cause.

  • Work with our runtime across Lambda, ECS and EKS, and help move more workloads onto Kubernetes.

  • Help operate the data and streaming infrastructure you depend on: Kafka, Flink, Redis/Valkey, RDS, Redshift.

  • Extend our infrastructure as code in AWS CDK, and our CI/CD pipelines.

  • Reduce toil. Automate the manual, delete the unnecessary, make the next incident less likely.


ABOUT YOU:

  • 4+ years as a software or reliability engineer, with production systems you’ve built and supported.

  • High ownership tendencies.

  • Genuine interest in both halves of this role. You want to write the service and own how it runs.

  • Strong in at least one of Kotlin, Java, Python or TypeScript.

  • A solid working understanding of AWS - compute, networking, storage, IAM - from running things in production.

  • Hands-on with infrastructure as code: AWS CDK, Terraform, CloudFormation or similar.

  • Practical experience running container workloads on Kubernetes: deploying, debugging, tuning.

  • Experience with CI/CD tooling and a clear view of a good delivery lifecycle.

  • A habit of instrumenting what you build - metrics, logging, tracing.

  • Experience being on the hook for production, incident response included, and calm when things are on fire.

  • Experience defining or working to service-level objectives, or a clear sense of how you’d start.

  • A strong urge to own and improve things - to spot what isn’t working and fix it.

  • Comfortable with agent-based development tools. We use Claude Code; any equivalent is fine.

  • A clear communicator and a pragmatic problem-solver.


NICE TO HAVE EXPERIENCE:

  • Building or operating a platform on Kubernetes, EKS especially.

  • Datadog specifically.

  • Data or streaming systems: Kafka, Flink, Redshift, clustered Postgres.

  • Working to error budgets, and using them to make real prioritisation calls.

  • Security and compliance best practice in cloud environments.

  • Complex distributed environments - high throughput, low latency, large datasets.

  • Any exposure to commodities, energy or financial markets. Useful, but we’ll teach you the domain.

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you.

If it's on you, it's in your control.

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift

Honesty is an expression of care.

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

We are determined that no-one will ever receive less favourable treatment on the grounds of gender, age, disability, religion, belief, sexual orientation, marital status, race, veteran status or any basis covered by appropriate law.

title: Global Investigator (Triage)
description: Build a Safer World. TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure. As a Global Investigator on the triage team, you will be the first line of operational defense in a fast-moving crypto disruption pipeline. You will process inbound complaint data, validate outputs from our artificial-intelligence (AI) investigation platform, and route cases into the investigative pipelines that result in frozen scam proceeds and seized assets. You will hold the disposition pen: your call is what turns a complaint into a freeze, a takedown, a recovery handoff, a legal-process draft, a victim notification, or a close. The impact you will have: Validate and route hundreds of complaint dispositions per week, feeding a live asset-recovery pipeline. Catch the AI errors that matter, such as false positives, merged syndicates, and misclassified scam patterns, before they propagate downstream. Enrich complaint selectors using a stack of more than forty commercial data-source integrations. Own clean shift handoffs so the around-the-clock operation never drops a lead, providing EMEA-hours coverage that keeps the queue moving while colleagues in other regions are offline. What we’re looking for: Investigative or analytical experience in the private or public sector. One to three years is fine: we want hungry people who want to grow into deep crypto expertise. Strong AI fluency, meaning comfort using AI tools as a daily co-pilot, plus the judgment to know when they are wrong. Excitement to deepen blockchain analysis skills. Comfort operating in a fast-paced, fluid environment where the project's scope and emphasis may shift quarter to quarter. Strong written and verbal communication. About the Team: The team is built around a mix of seasoned investigators and rising talent. Triage investigators sit alongside experienced crypto tracers and intelligence-trained individual contributors, and the seat is designed to accelerate your development. Team Operating Rhythms: Daily schedule: standard business hours in your local time zone. Collaboration: coordinate with global teammates for handoffs on time-sensitive items, giving the wider operation near follow-the-sun coverage. On-Call Responsibilities: Formal on-call rotation for high-priority events, such as hacks, law-enforcement support, and other time-sensitive matters. Weekly rotation, with occasional weekend coverage as needed. Learn about TRM Speed in this position: React quickly to incoming complaint surges and live takedown events. Continuously learn new patterns in crypto-enabled crime. Application Instructions If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team. Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role. If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered. Interviewing with TRM Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview. Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role. Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact. First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role. Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM. References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact. Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details. Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you! Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way. AI Fluency at TRM AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM. We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks. At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to: Accelerate repeatable workflows Structure and solve problems Improve output quality Increase speed and leverage You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process. Life at TRM We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day. TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days. Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving. At TRM, you should expect: Priorities and targets to change quickly Operating with a high degree of ambiguity A high level of personal ownership and accountability Close collaboration across teams and functions Frequent, high-touch communication Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment. We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here. TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. As a Global Investigator on the triage team, you will be the first line of operational defense in a fast-moving crypto disruption pipeline. You will process inbound complaint data, validate outputs from our artificial-intelligence (AI) investigation platform, and route cases into the investigative pipelines that result in frozen scam proceeds and seized assets. You will hold the disposition pen: your call is what turns a complaint into a freeze, a takedown, a recovery handoff, a legal-process draft, a victim notification, or a close.

The impact you will have:

  • Validate and route hundreds of complaint dispositions per week, feeding a live asset-recovery pipeline.

  • Catch the AI errors that matter, such as false positives, merged syndicates, and misclassified scam patterns, before they propagate downstream.

  • Enrich complaint selectors using a stack of more than forty commercial data-source integrations.

  • Own clean shift handoffs so the around-the-clock operation never drops a lead, providing EMEA-hours coverage that keeps the queue moving while colleagues in other regions are offline.

What we’re looking for:

  • Investigative or analytical experience in the private or public sector. One to three years is fine: we want hungry people who want to grow into deep crypto expertise.

  • Strong AI fluency, meaning comfort using AI tools as a daily co-pilot, plus the judgment to know when they are wrong.

  • Excitement to deepen blockchain analysis skills.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced, fluid environment where the project's scope and emphasis may shift quarter to quarter.

  • Strong written and verbal communication.

  • Collaboration: coordinate with global teammates for handoffs on time-sensitive items, giving the wider operation near follow-the-sun coverage.

  • Formal on-call rotation for high-priority events, such as hacks, law-enforcement support, and other time-sensitive matters.

description: À propos de nous Chez Upvest, notre mission est de rendre l’investissement aussi simple que dépenser de l’argent. Upvest permet aux entreprises de proposer une large gamme de produits d’investissement et la meilleure expérience en matière d’investissement sur les marchés de capitaux et d’épargne retraite. Notre Investment API s’intègre facilement, pour que les fintechs et les institutions financières puissent se concentrer pleinement sur leur cœur de métier. Nous travaillons avec les principales fintechs et institutions financières européennes, comme DKB, Revolut, N26 et Raisin. Fondée en 2017 par Martin Kassing, Upvest réunit aujourd’hui plus de 270 professionnels de plus de 70 nationalités. Upvest a levé 280 M€ auprès d’investisseurs de premier plan, dont BlackRock, Tencent, Sapphire Ventures, Bessemer Venture Partners, Earlybird, Notion Capital et Motive. Notre dernier tour de table de 105 M€, en mars 2026 et mené par Sapphire et Tencent, accélère notre croissance et nous permet d’offrir une expérience d’investissement haut de gamme. Le poste En 2027, Upvest lance le Plan d’Épargne en Actions (PEA) sur le marché français avec plusieurs fintechs de premier plan. Au sein de l’équipe Settlements & Transfers, vous intervenez sur l’ensemble de la chaîne post-marché des transferts de comptes-titres et de PEA : du traitement des instructions au dénouement chez Euroclear France, en passant par les relations avec les teneurs de compte, les dépositaires et les émetteurs. Ce stage vous offre une exposition directe au post-marché français et européen dans une phase de lancement, avec de réelles responsabilités dès les premières semaines. Vos missions Transferts entrants et sortants : Prendre en charge les transferts de comptes-titres (CTO) et de PEA avec les banques et courtiers en France et en Europe, de la réception de la demande jusqu’au dénouement des titres et des espèces. Relations contreparties et clients : Assurer une communication fluide avec les contreparties (banques, courtiers, dépositaires) et nos clients, et piloter le suivi des demandes et des relances. Contrôles et réconciliations : Vérifier les positions titres et espèces, rapprocher les mouvements avec notre dépositaire et analyser les écarts. Gestion des suspens et des anomalies : Analyser les instructions non dénouées ou rejetées, en identifier l’origine et coordonner leur résolution avec les contreparties et les équipes internes. Fiscalité du PEA : Contrôler et intégrer les bordereaux d’information (BI) afin de garantir la continuité de l’historique fiscal du plan. Titres au nominatif : Traiter les opérations sur titres nominatifs (conversions, inscriptions, radiations). Reporting et amélioration continue : Suivre activement les SLA et les KPI, rédiger les procédures et identifier des pistes d’automatisation. Votre profil Formation : Master 1 ou 2 en finance, banque, économie ou droit (école de commerce, d’ingénieurs ou université), en année de césure ou jeune diplômé(e) d’un Master, avec possibilité de signer une convention de stage. Pour les M1 : votre établissement doit permettre un stage de 6 mois à temps plein (semestre intégré ou dispense de cours). Langues : Français langue maternelle (indispensable) et anglais courant. Expérience : Une première expérience en banque, back-office, middle-office ou opérations titres est un réel atout, tout comme une connaissance du PEA, du post-marché ou d’Euroclear France. Motivation : Un véritable intérêt pour les marchés de capitaux et les opérations post-marché. Esprit d’analyse : Rigueur, sens du détail et goût pour la résolution de problèmes complexes. Outils : Bonne maîtrise d’Excel / Google Sheets ; la connaissance de SQL/Python est un plus. Pourquoi nous rejoindre Un travail à fort impact : Nous construisons l’infrastructure qui portera l’avenir de l’investissement en Europe. C’est complexe, ambitieux et porteur de sens. Vous travaillerez avec des technologies modernes et créerez quelque chose de totalement nouveau, sans système hérité et sans limites. Moments d’équipe : Participez aux événements d’entreprise comme UpFest, les dîners, les offsites et la fête de fin d’année, pour échanger avec vos collègues et célébrer nos réussites. Inclusion : Nous nous engageons pour une culture où chacun a sa place et s’épanouit. Nos groupes de ressources pour les employés favorisent l’inclusion et les liens, comme Upfem Black at Upvest, Up&Out et UpVergent. Nos valeurs Make it easy for others. Nous simplifions le complexe et agissons avec les meilleures intentions. Own the outcome. Nous sommes proactifs, rapides et confiants pour faire avancer les choses : le progrès avant la perfection. Rise to the challenge. Nous visons haut et repoussons les limites. Nous restons curieux, apprenons et célébrons nos réussites ensemble. Tell the story. Nous commençons par le « pourquoi ». Nous sommes transparents et partageons nos connaissances pour inspirer les autres. Upvest garantit l’égalité des chances. Nous célébrons la diversité et nous nous engageons à créer un environnement inclusif pour tous. À compétences égales, tous nos postes sont ouverts aux personnes en situation de handicap. title: Director of Engineering
description: Who we are Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables. We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi . The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level. We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter , Noah Hollmann , and Sauraj Gambhir , and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun. In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years. The role You will be our first dedicated engineering leader, reporting to the CTO with a direct line to both founders - no layers in between. Today, engineering at Prior Labs is a small, very senior team. We plan to grow it substantially over the next 18 months, and your job is to build and run that organization. We want to be honest about what this job is. It is a hands-on operator role: managing engineers, building the hiring machine, setting standards, running compliance, and working closely with our partners at SAP. If you light up at making an organization fast rather than at owning the biggest possible headcount, this is your role. What you'll do Directly manage and grow the engineering team, including building out its management layer. Build the hiring machine: run hiring operations across our hiring managers, design interview loops that hold up in the AI era, and keep a very high bar while the team grows. Own engineering standards and velocity: how we review, test, and ship - and how the team gets real leverage from AI coding tools. Own our security and compliance program - SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001 - right-sized, so the lab keeps its speed. Own the engineering side of our collaboration with SAP. Treat the deployment layer as a product surface: our models reach customers through a managed API, customer VPCs, and self-hosted open weights, and the engineering behind that needs customer empathy, not just platform craft. Act as a sparring partner to the founders on org design and engineering direction - we're hiring someone who will argue with us. What we're looking for You have directly led an engineering organization of 10+ people, including through managers or leads, and you can talk concretely about how you built it. You have owned platform or infrastructure scope at scale: serving, APIs, availability, cloud and vendor budgets. You have worked in both startups and large organizations - you can create structure from scratch and hold your own with a very large partner. You scaled an engineering org through a real growth phase (25 to 60+ or similar), building the management layer along the way. You have led engineering in a research- or ML-heavy organization and know how research code and production code differ - and how to bridge them without slowing research down. What sets you apart You have led engineering through an acquisition, working directly with the parent company. You have personally changed how your team works because of AI coding tools, and can show what it did to output. You have operated under SOC 2 / ISO-style audit regimes; having built or run the function yourself is a plus. Life at Prior Labs You'll work alongside researchers and builders who hold themselves to a very high bar - in the quality of their work and in how they work with each other. We move fast and still take the time to do things right. Our teams are based in Berlin, Freiburg, and New York - when you're working on something as hard as TabPFN, being in the same room matters. But great people come from everywhere, and in exceptional cases we're open to remote, which usually means frequent travel to one of our offices. Wherever you're based, the whole company comes together regularly for offsites to build and celebrate together. Our Commitments The best products and teams are built by people with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds. We welcome applications from all identities and walks of life - especially if you've ever felt discouraged by "not checking every box" - and provide equal opportunities regardless of gender, sexual orientation, origin, disability, or any other trait that makes you who you are.
